newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 10.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Ramos on Sunday extended until April the government's unilateral ceasfire with communist insurgents as part of government's confidence-building efforts to strengthen its peace and development programmes. (INQUIRER/MALAYA/JOURNAL)

- The amend-the-Charter drive is facing another major roadblock as the Palace said on Sunday the May 12 town elections may still be postponed because of a pending petition in the Supreme Court questioning the legality of holding the polls this year. (STANDARD/CHRONICLE)

- The Citizens' Action Against Crime and the Movement for the Restoration of Peace and Order yesterday said kidnapping in the country is getting worse, with 41 persons victimized from January to March 7. (MALAYA)

- The Department of Finance has expressed concern over possible revenue losses by the national government between 37 billion and 40 billion pesos if Congress would push through with its plan to raise the exemption level for each individual taxpayer to 72,000 pesos. (TODAY/INQUIRER)

- Victorias Milling Co Inc, which is facing a serious problem paying off some 6.6 billion pesos in loans owed to several banks, will have to negotiate a loan accommodation with each of its creditor banks, Metrobank president Antonio Abacan said. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
